classes.locator: https://www.arlis.am/hy/acts/143723/latest (Art. 89(1): at least 101 deputies; Art. 89(3): elected by the proportional system; Art. 90(1): five-year term)
classes.finest_note: Precinct protocols as spreadsheets from 2007 (resultarm.xls) to 2026; 1999 and 2003 only as national summary protocols; 1995 not published by the CEC. Four seats go to the national minorities named in Electoral Code Art. 95(9), filled from the second part of the party lists, not by a separate vote.
classes.note: From 1995 to 2012 the nationwide list tier elected 40 (1995), 56 (1999), 75 (2003), and 90 (2007, 2012) members beside single-member districts; since the 2016 Electoral Code the whole Assembly is elected from party lists, with bonus seats for a stable majority (Art. 96) and a second round between the top two when no majority forms (Art. 98, never yet held). In 2017 voters also cast a preference vote for district list candidates in 13 territorial districts.

dates.note: First National Assembly election, held with the constitutional referendum; the CEC publishes no results for it.

classes.name_en: President of the Republic, elected by the National Assembly (from 2018)
classes.locator: https://www.arlis.am/hy/acts/143723/latest (Art. 124(1): seven-year term; Art. 125(1): «Հանրապետության նախագահն ընտրվում է Ազգային ժողովի կողմից»)
classes.note: Deputies vote by secret ballot; a candidate needs three quarters of all deputies in the first round, three fifths in a second, and a majority of votes cast in the third (Art. 125). Held on 2 March 2018 and, after a resignation, on 3 March 2022. The National Assembly, not the CEC, records the votes.

classes.note: Constitutional amendments, laws proposed by citizens' initiative and rejected by the Assembly, and questions of membership in supranational organizations or of territory go to referendum (Constitution Arts. 202, 204, 205). The referendum called for 5 April 2020 on the Constitutional Court was suspended under the COVID-19 state of emergency and never held; the CEC page keeps its preparation files only.

dates.note: The independence referendum of 21 September 1991 and the constitutional referendum of 5 July 1995 (the Constitution's own title dates it «1995 թվականի հուլիսի 5»); the CEC publishes no results for them.

classes.name: Հայաստանի Հանրապետության Գերագույն խորհուրդ
classes.name_en: Supreme Council of the Republic of Armenia (Armenian SSR to 1990), 1990-1995
classes.note: Elected in single-member districts from 20 May 1990 with later rounds and repeat polls; it declared independence and served until the first National Assembly of 1995.
classes.disposition_reason: No official body publishes the 1990 district results: the CEC's archive begins in 1999, and the returns survive only in the contemporary press and the National Archives.

classes.name: Հայկական ՍՍՀ Գերագույն խորհուրդ
classes.name_en: Supreme Soviet of the Armenian SSR, 1938-1985
classes.note: Single-candidate district elections every four, later five, years under the 1937 and 1978 constitutions of the Armenian SSR; the local soviets were elected the same way.
classes.disposition_reason: Results were printed only in the official press of the time; no current official body publishes them, and the CEC's archive begins in 1999.

classes.name: Հայաստանի Հանրապետության Խորհրդարան
classes.name_en: Parliament of the First Republic of Armenia, 1919
classes.note: The First Republic's only general election, by party lists on 21-23 June 1919; the Republic ended with the Soviet takeover of 2 December 1920.
classes.disposition_reason: No official body publishes the 1919 returns; they survive in the National Archives of Armenia and the press of the time, neither reachable as an official results publication.

classes.name: Ազգային փոքրամասնությունների մանդատներ
classes.name_en: National minority seats in the National Assembly
classes.locator: https://www.arlis.am/hy/acts/105967/latest (Art. 83(5)-(6) and Art. 95(9): four seats, one each for the four largest national minorities, from the second part of the party lists)
classes.disposition_reason: There is no separate minority vote: the four seats are allocated from the second part of the nationwide party lists, so they are counted in the National Assembly list contest.

classes.name: Ազգային ժողովի կողմից ընտրվող պաշտոնատար անձինք
classes.name_en: Officers elected by the National Assembly (Prime Minister, Speaker, Constitutional Court judges, Human Rights Defender)
classes.disposition_reason: Parliamentary votes on officers are part of the Assembly's proceedings, not elections run by an electoral authority; no judge, prosecutor, or police officer is elected by voters.

classes.name: Կուսակցությունների թեկնածուների առաջադրում
classes.locator: https://www.arlis.am/hy/acts/105967/latest (Art. 83(8): lists approved by the party congress or its standing governing body)
classes.disposition_reason: Parties approve their lists at congresses under their own rules; the state neither runs nor publishes any nominating contest.

classes.name: Համայնքի ղեկավարի ընտրություններ
classes.locator: https://www.arlis.am/hy/acts/105967/latest (Art. 104.1(2)(1): one single-member district per community; Art. 104.1(4): majoritarian in communities of up to 4,000 voters)
classes.finest_note: Each poll's page gives candidates and per-precinct protocol figures; reached by form posts with the election id.
classes.note: Plurality, five-year term (Constitution Art. 181(1)). Regular polls fall on up to four days a year set by the CEC (Electoral Code Art. 122(1)); extraordinary polls follow vacancies. Before 2009 the 12 districts of Yerevan were communities and elected heads here; since 2009 Yerevan's mayor, and since 2021 the head of every community over 4,000 voters, is chosen by the council (community_head_council).

dates.note: Local self-government elections of 1996, 1999, and 2002 and the by-elections between them; the CEC publishes no list or results for polls before 2005.

classes.name: Տեղական հանրաքվեներ
classes.note: Constitution Art. 183(1) lets residents decide community questions by local referendum. The 22 polls of 17 May 2015 put the merger of communities in Lori (around Tumanyan), Tavush (around Dilijan), and Syunik (around Tatev) to the vote: «Համաձայն ե՞ք, որպեսզի Թումանյան, Մարց, ... համայնքները միավորվեն».

dates.quote: 17.05.2015: 22 local referendums in the list
